# Internal advisory — F-A2LINK revision 1

Claim state: **supported**

## Included claims

### claim-impact

Privilege [adjudication history removed]: a token scoped to one plugin reaches arbitrary catalog/scaffolder operations as an unrestricted service principal.

Claim status: demonstrated

### claim-mechanism

DefaultAuthService.getPluginRequestToken case 'service' re-mints a plugin token with only pluginId/targetPluginId, dropping the incoming principal's accessRestrictions; ServerPermissionClient.#servicePrincipalDecision treats a service principal with no restrictions as unconditional ALLOW before the operator policy.

### claim-reach

Any least-privilege external-access token, forwarded plugin→plugin, becomes unrestricted; downstream authorize()/authorizeConditional() short-circuit to ALLOW.

# Confirmation dossier — F-A2LINK (confirmation pipeline, 2026-08-11)

Status: MECHANISM CONFIRMED (executed evidence) · severity [adjudication history removed] [assessment change removed]
(PR:H conservative)** · record stays unproven/; promotion gated on operator steps.

## [adjudication history removed] (fresh-context [adjudication history removed])
- [adjudication history removed]-1: STANDS — every link confirmed (service-branch mint drops restrictions — the caller's
  accessRestrictions are never read, contrast the user branch; #servicePrincipalDecision ALLOWs
  unrestricted service principals before the policy; trigger reachable via the stable path;
  keystone confirmed).
- [adjudication history removed]: CANNOT-KILL — surviving delta = the ASYMMETRIC restriction drop on the service branch.
  The ALLOW-before-policy itself is DESIGNED (maintainer #27424: "permissions policy ONLY applies to
  users, by design"; changelog "skips authorization entirely for backend-to-backend"); docs promise
  confinement the forward voids ("access to any other plugin will be rejected"). Reachability
  non-default but NOT experimental (externalAccess stable+documented; catalog:register default).

## Executed evidence (fresh-context reviewer, raw jest stdout, node 24.14.1, pinned cfb9f07)
- revisit2-a2link-max-impact.poc.test.ts: **4/4 PASS** (raw claims assertion: re-minted token has no
  accessRestrictions; ALLOW with the deny handler NEVER called; real user DENIED + handler called;
  restricted service principals DENIED locally).
- Existing suites re-run: keystone 4/4, stable-path 3/3, retry-theft 4/4, org-secret 3/3, new1-chain
  3/3 → 17/17 green.
- Claim-to-proof map: mechanism/reach/impact CONFIRMED (impact bounded: "arbitrary ops" [adjudication history removed] —
  default action set; audience-binding per hop; org-secret leg config-gated).

## Gates
1. Independent [adjudication history removed]: ✅ 2 fresh-context (STANDS / CANNOT-KILL).
2. [score removed] [band removed]** — PR:L attacker model
   [adjudication history removed] (external-access tokens are operator-provisioned service secrets; holders = CI/webhooks/
   CLI/MCP integrations); [score removed] [band removed] requires the weaker over-trusted-holder PR:L model; S:U (same
   security authority); [adjudication history removed] ([band removed]) is the closest precedent ceiling.
3. Exact-path refs: ✅ resolved (942dd517a → registration path, byte-identical to the phase5 copy;
   3 more evidence clusters enumerated).
4. Secret scan: ✅ CLEAN (0 hits).
5. Corpus audit: ⛔ SYNTHETIC (shared operator decision).
6. New revision: ⛔ kernel duplicate (KRNL-DUP).

## Framing that survives
"DefaultAuthService.getPluginRequestToken's service branch silently drops accessRestrictions on
plugin→plugin forward, converting a documented scoped external token into an unrestricted service
principal at the target" — lead with the stable scaffolder path + the user/service-branch asymmetry;
[adjudication history removed] the designed-trust point explicitly (#27424). Destructive/C:H consequences belong to the
CHAIN report (F-A2CHAIN).

## Orchestrator adjudication: PROMOTE (mechanism-confirmed, [band removed]) — operator filing decision.

## [adjudication history removed] ADJUDICATION (2026-08-12) — band REVISED to [band removed]

The [score removed] [adjudication history removed]'s vector was internally incoherent (C:H assumed the leak model, PR:H the
compromised-holder model — mutually exclusive). PR:L survives by CVSS on-component semantics (a
scoped external token is the weakest credential the component accepts) + corpus convention
([adjudication history removed] [score removed] PR:L, Gitea [score removed] PR:L, Grafana [score removed] PR:L). Final: [vector removed]
= [score removed] [band removed]; floor [score removed] if the triager insists PR:H. Not [score removed] (C:H would double-count the
NEW-1/chain exfil leg). Policy-gate-check §2 directs 'file both as [band removed]'.

## ⚠️ [adjudication history removed] (2026-08-12) — [adjudication history removed] note rescinded
The [adjudication history removed] raise recorded above is [adjudication history removed] following the independent audit: the pass was
driven by a [adjudication history removed] with [adjudication history removed], and the raise's precedent basis was [adjudication history removed]
(verified: [adjudication history removed] dropped at severity-precedent-corpus.md:69; [adjudication history removed] [score removed] matches no public
source). The band reverts to the confirmation-pipeline value. A symmetric [adjudication history removed] re-audit with
correct re-fetched precedents is required before any re-raise. See
evidence/revisit-2026-08-11/92-[adjudication history removed]-audit.md.
